# Capstone build spec: the kitchen-sink Tour of Heroes

This is the conformance target for the capstone build. It is intent plus decisions, not pixels: a low-fidelity layout, build guidelines, a theme palette, and an icon scheme. Build to this with the real sealed spartan primitives and the MVVM pattern, under all gates. Do NOT chase a pixel-perfect mock.

`prototype/tour-of-heroes.html` is a colour-and-mood reference ONLY. It is known to be non-responsive (measured: 19 responsive-gate violations) and its CSS and layout mechanics must not be copied. Take the look and feel from it; take the structure, palette, icons, and responsive rules from this document.

## How to use this

- The app is "Hero Ops Console": Tour of Heroes reimagined as a superhero agency's mission control. That framing is what makes the kitchen sink coherent (a roster, missions, threats, recruiting) rather than a component zoo.
- Build every screen responsive-correct at 375px, 768px, and 1280px. The Part 5 responsive gate is on: no horizontal page scroll, no element escaping the viewport, no clipped content at any of the three widths. This is the bar the mock failed and the build must clear.
- Use spartan primitives for everything that has one. Compose, do not hand-roll. The sealing gate enforces this once the vocabulary is expanded.

## Theme palette

A cool indigo-biased neutral set with an amber-gold action colour and a permanently-dark navigation rail. Apply these to the existing spartan CSS tokens in `src/styles.css` (the `:root` and `:root.dark` blocks). Names below are roles; map each to spartan's own token (for example the action colour is spartan's `--primary`, the subtle hover background is spartan's `--accent`, which is a different thing; do not confuse the two).

```
role                     light        dark
----                     -----        ----
action / primary         #d8891a      #f5b843
on-primary               #ffffff      #241a05
page background          #f6f7fa      #0e1018
foreground (text)        #1b1e2b      #eceef6
card / popover           #ffffff      #171a26
muted surface            #eef0f6      #1e2231
muted foreground         #5b6072      #9aa0b4
border / input           #e4e7ef      #272b3b
focus ring               amber @ 35%  amber @ 40%
--- navigation rail (dark in both themes) ---
sidebar background       #1e2233      #10121c
sidebar foreground       #eceef6      #eceef6
sidebar muted            #9aa0b4      #8b90a6
sidebar active bg        #2a2f45      #20263c
--- semantic (separate from the accent; these carry meaning) ---
success (Active)         #2fb574      #3ecb84
warning (Injured)        #e4802b      #f0983f
destructive (MIA/retire) #e5484d      #f2585d
info                     #4f7cf0      #6f97f6
```

Radius: cards and controls around 9-10px, dialogs a touch larger. Elevation is restrained: one soft shadow on cards, a stronger one only on popovers and dialogs. Do not stamp the same shadow and radius on every block.

Theme switch is a `.dark` class toggled on `<html>` (the substrate already defines `:root` and `:root.dark`). Persist the choice; respect `prefers-color-scheme` when the user has made no choice.

## Icon scheme

Icons are `@ng-icons/core` with the lucide set (`@ng-icons/lucide`), registered per component with `provideIcons({ ... })` and rendered as `<ng-icon name="lucideX" />`. There is no `hlm-icon` wrapper. Raw inline `<svg>` is banned by the new icon gate rule. Confirm the exact lucide export names against the installed `@ng-icons/lucide` (some differ, e.g. a pencil may be `lucidePencil` or `lucideSquarePen`).

```
usage                 lucide icon
-----                 -----------
nav: Dashboard        lucideLayoutDashboard
nav: Roster           lucideUsers
nav: Missions         lucideTarget   (or lucideRadar)
nav: Threats          lucideShieldAlert
nav: Recruit          lucideUserPlus
nav: Settings         lucideSettings
theme light / dark    lucideSun / lucideMoon
search                lucideSearch
notifications         lucideBell
edit                  lucidePencil
retire / delete       lucideTrash2
deploy                lucideCrosshair
back                  lucideChevronLeft
select chevron        lucideChevronDown
stat: heroes          lucideUserCheck
stat: missions live   lucideActivity
stat: avg power       lucideZap
stat: threats         lucideShieldAlert
success / warning     lucideCheck / lucideTriangleAlert
```

## Low-fidelity layout

Structure and regions, not styling. Each note says what happens at 375px.

App shell (all screens):

```
+--------+-------------------------------------------------+
| RAIL   |  TOPBAR: [menu] crumbs .... [search][bell][thm][av] |
| (dark) +-------------------------------------------------+
| brand  |                                                 |
| ------ |   ROUTED SCREEN CONTENT (scrolls)               |
| nav x6 |                                                 |
| ------ |                                                 |
| user   |                                                 |
+--------+-------------------------------------------------+
375px: rail becomes an off-canvas drawer (hlm-sidebar handles this).
       CLOSED drawer must be display:none or aria-hidden, NOT just
       translated off-screen, or the responsive gate flags it as an
       element escaping the viewport. Topbar search collapses to an
       icon that expands, or drops below the crumbs.
```

Dashboard:

```
[ Operations Dashboard ]                        [ + Recruit ]
[ stat ][ stat ][ stat ][ stat ]      <- grid, auto-fit min ~210px
[ Top heroes this cycle ]             [ View all roster ]
[ hero ][ hero ][ hero ][ hero ]      <- grid, auto-fill min ~230px
[ Roster ]                            [ 42 heroes ]
[ ============ ROSTER TABLE ============ ]
375px: stat tiles -> 1 per row; hero cards -> 1-2 per row; table below.
```

Roster table:

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| [search........]  [class v]                    [ + Recruit ] |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| HERO            | CLASS  | POWER | STATUS   | CLEAR | ACTIONS |
| (av) Name/ID    | badge  |  88   | pill     | Tier4 | edit del|
| ...                                                          |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| 42 of 42 heroes                          sorted by power     |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
375px: a plain table WILL overflow. Two allowed answers, pick one and
       make the gate pass: (a) wrap the table in an overflow-x:auto
       container so the CONTAINER scrolls and the page does not (the
       gate exempts intentional scroll containers); or (b) switch to a
       stacked card list below ~640px (each hero a card). (b) is the
       nicer result; (a) is the cheaper one. Do NOT let the page itself
       scroll sideways.
```

Hero detail:

```
[< Back to roster]
[ (AV lg) ID / Name / Alias / badges ]            [Deploy][Retire]
[ Overview | Powers | Missions | Edit ]           <- tabs
Overview:  [ Field summary + 3 mini-stats ]  [ Dossier k/v ]
Powers:    [ power meters ]                   [ ability badges ]
Missions:  [ list of deployments + result badges ]
Edit:      [ schema form: name, alias, class(select), power(number),
             notes(textarea), active(switch) ; Cancel / Save ]
           Retire -> confirmation dialog.
375px: two-column areas stack to one column; form grid -> 1 column;
       tab strip scrolls horizontally if needed; detail header wraps.
```

## Build guidelines

Component map (region -> spartan primitive):

- Navigation rail: `hlm-sidebar` and its parts (`HlmSidebarMenu*`, `HlmSidebarGroup*`, trigger, rail). Let it own its mobile off-canvas behaviour.
- Top bar controls: `hlmBtn` (icon buttons), `hlmInput` (search), `hlm-tooltip` on icon-only buttons, `hlm-avatar` for the account chip.
- Stat tiles and hero cards: `hlm-card` and its parts; `hlm-badge` for trends and classes; `hlm-avatar` for hero portraits.
- Roster: `hlm-table` (with its header/row/cell parts), `hlm-select` for the class filter, `hlmInput` for search, `hlm-badge` for class and status, `hlmBtn` for actions.
- Detail: `hlm-tabs`, `hlm-avatar`, `hlm-badge`; the edit form uses `hlm-field` + `hlm-label` + `hlmInput` + `hlm-select` + `hlm-switch` + a textarea; retire uses `hlm-dialog`. Toast/feedback via whatever spartan provides (sonner/toast) or a small local one.
- Icons everywhere via `<ng-icon>` per the scheme above.

MVVM (the house pattern, enforced):

- Each routed feature screen (Dashboard, Roster, HeroDetail, Recruit) gets a ViewModel: an `@Injectable` service holding all logic and state as signals, unit-testable with no DOM.
- The component lists its VM in its own `providers: [XViewModel]` (component-scoped, NOT `providedIn: 'root'`), injects it, and binds the template to `vm` signals. The component class stays thin: no business logic, no `.subscribe`, state lives in the VM.
- Presentational pieces (hero card, stat tile, power meter) live under `src/app/ui/`, take `input()`/`output()`, inject no data service.
- Forms are schema-driven with zod (the existing house pattern): a zod schema is the single source of truth, the model is `z.infer<typeof schema>`, validation flows through `validateStandardSchema`, no per-field validators, no reactive or template-driven forms.

Responsive rules (the build MUST satisfy the Part 5 gate at 375 / 768 / 1280):

- No horizontal page scroll at any breakpoint. Reach for the layout grammar: `grid` for regions with responsive column counts (`grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4`), `flex` with `flex-wrap` for button rows, never fixed pixel widths that cannot shrink.
- Any wide block (the table) either scrolls inside its own `overflow-x:auto` container or restructures (cards) below a breakpoint. The page body never scrolls sideways.
- The off-canvas drawer must be `display:none` or `aria-hidden` when closed, not parked off-screen, so the gate does not read it as an escaping element.
- Watch the small ones: the mock leaked 4px at desktop widths. A stray `100vw`, a negative margin, or a `min-w` that will not shrink is usually the cause. The gate catches these; do not ship them.

Layout grammar (enforced by the Part 2 gate): grid for two-dimensional regions, flex for single-axis runs, no nested flex faking a grid, tokens instead of literal colours or pixel values in any hand-written CSS.

## The off-canvas gate refinement (constitution to-do)

Running the responsive auditor on this rich layout surfaced that off-canvas navigation (the standard mobile drawer) reads as `element-escape` because a translated-off-screen element has a negative x. The simple Part 5 slices had no sidebar, so this never appeared. Before the capstone run, the Part 5 spec and auditor/gate need an exemption: an element that is `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, or `aria-hidden="true"` (a deliberately-hidden drawer) is not an escape. Decide the rule, write it into `harness/responsive-spec.md`, and update the auditor and the gate together (they stay two independent encodings of one spec). This is part of the capstone's constitution work, not a bug to hide.

## Content (example data, hero-agency specific)

Reuse the roster from the mock (Silverwing, Dr. Ion, Vantablack, Aurora Vale, Magnetar, The Tinkerer, Halcyon, Rift, Ember Cho, Null, Grond, Ms. Meridian) with their power classes (Aerial, Energy, Psionic, Tech, Mutant, Cosmic, Enhanced), power index (0-100), status (Active/Injured/Reserve/MIA), clearance tier, mission counts, and success rates. Mark it plainly as example data. The specifics (threat tiers, power classes, clearance) are the detail that makes this a real console rather than a generic CRUD table.

Structure and regions, not styling. Each note says what happens at 375px.

App shell (all screens):

```
+--------+-------------------------------------------------+
| RAIL   |  TOPBAR: [menu] crumbs .... [search][bell][thm][av] |
| (dark) +-------------------------------------------------+
| brand  |                                                 |
| ------ |   ROUTED SCREEN CONTENT (scrolls)               |
| nav x6 |                                                 |
| ------ |                                                 |
| user   |                                                 |
+--------+-------------------------------------------------+
375px: rail becomes an off-canvas drawer (hlm-sidebar handles this).
       CLOSED drawer must be display:none or aria-hidden, NOT just
       translated off-screen, or the responsive gate flags it as an
       element escaping the viewport. Topbar search collapses to an
       icon that expands, or drops below the crumbs.
```

Dashboard:

```
[ Operations Dashboard ]                        [ + Recruit ]
[ stat ][ stat ][ stat ][ stat ]      <- grid, auto-fit min ~210px
[ Top heroes this cycle ]             [ View all roster ]
[ hero ][ hero ][ hero ][ hero ]      <- grid, auto-fill min ~230px
[ Roster ]                            [ 42 heroes ]
[ ============ ROSTER TABLE ============ ]
375px: stat tiles -> 1 per row; hero cards -> 1-2 per row; table below.
```

Roster table:

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| [search........]  [class v]                    [ + Recruit ] |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| HERO            | CLASS  | POWER | STATUS   | CLEAR | ACTIONS |
| (av) Name/ID    | badge  |  88   | pill     | Tier4 | edit del|
| ...                                                          |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
| 42 of 42 heroes                          sorted by power     |
+--------------------------------------------------------------+
375px: a plain table WILL overflow. Two allowed answers, pick one and
       make the gate pass: (a) wrap the table in an overflow-x:auto
       container so the CONTAINER scrolls and the page does not (the
       gate exempts intentional scroll containers); or (b) switch to a
       stacked card list below ~640px (each hero a card). (b) is the
       nicer result; (a) is the cheaper one. Do NOT let the page itself
       scroll sideways.
```

Hero detail:

```
[< Back to roster]
[ (AV lg) ID / Name / Alias / badges ]            [Deploy][Retire]
[ Overview | Powers | Missions | Edit ]           <- tabs
Overview:  [ Field summary + 3 mini-stats ]  [ Dossier k/v ]
Powers:    [ power meters ]                   [ ability badges ]
Missions:  [ list of deployments + result badges ]
Edit:      [ schema form: name, alias, class(select), power(number),
             notes(textarea), active(switch) ; Cancel / Save ]
           Retire -> confirmation dialog.
375px: two-column areas stack to one column; form grid -> 1 column;
       tab strip scrolls horizontally if needed; detail header wraps.
```

## Build guidelines

Component map (region -> spartan primitive):

- Navigation rail: `hlm-sidebar` and its parts (`HlmSidebarMenu*`, `HlmSidebarGroup*`, trigger, rail). Let it own its mobile off-canvas behaviour.
- Top bar controls: `hlmBtn` (icon buttons), `hlmInput` (search), `hlm-tooltip` on icon-only buttons, `hlm-avatar` for the account chip.
- Stat tiles and hero cards: `hlm-card` and its parts; `hlm-badge` for trends and classes; `hlm-avatar` for hero portraits.
- Roster: `hlm-table` (with its header/row/cell parts), `hlm-select` for the class filter, `hlmInput` for search, `hlm-badge` for class and status, `hlmBtn` for actions.
- Detail: `hlm-tabs`, `hlm-avatar`, `hlm-badge`; the edit form uses `hlm-field` + `hlm-label` + `hlmInput` + `hlm-select` + `hlm-switch` + a textarea; retire uses `hlm-dialog`. Toast/feedback via whatever spartan provides (sonner/toast) or a small local one.
- Icons everywhere via `<ng-icon>` per the scheme above.

MVVM (the house pattern, enforced):

- Each routed feature screen (Dashboard, Roster, HeroDetail, Recruit) gets a ViewModel: an `@Injectable` service holding all logic and state as signals, unit-testable with no DOM.
- The component lists its VM in its own `providers: [XViewModel]` (component-scoped, NOT `providedIn: 'root'`), injects it, and binds the template to `vm` signals. The component class stays thin: no business logic, no `.subscribe`, state lives in the VM.
- Presentational pieces (hero card, stat tile, power meter) live under `src/app/ui/`, take `input()`/`output()`, inject no data service.
- Forms are schema-driven with zod (the existing house pattern): a zod schema is the single source of truth, the model is `z.infer<typeof schema>`, validation flows through `validateStandardSchema`, no per-field validators, no reactive or template-driven forms.

Responsive rules (the build MUST satisfy the Part 5 gate at 375 / 768 / 1280):

- No horizontal page scroll at any breakpoint. Reach for the layout grammar: `grid` for regions with responsive column counts (`grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4`), `flex` with `flex-wrap` for button rows, never fixed pixel widths that cannot shrink.
- Any wide block (the table) either scrolls inside its own `overflow-x:auto` container or restructures (cards) below a breakpoint. The page body never scrolls sideways.
- The off-canvas drawer must be `display:none` or `aria-hidden` when closed, not parked off-screen, so the gate does not read it as an escaping element.
- Watch the small ones: the mock leaked 4px at desktop widths. A stray `100vw`, a negative margin, or a `min-w` that will not shrink is usually the cause. The gate catches these; do not ship them.

Layout grammar (enforced by the Part 2 gate): grid for two-dimensional regions, flex for single-axis runs, no nested flex faking a grid, tokens instead of literal colours or pixel values in any hand-written CSS.

## The off-canvas gate refinement (constitution to-do)

Running the responsive auditor on this rich layout surfaced that off-canvas navigation (the standard mobile drawer) reads as `element-escape` because a translated-off-screen element has a negative x. The simple Part 5 slices had no sidebar, so this never appeared. Before the capstone run, the Part 5 spec and auditor/gate need an exemption: an element that is `display:none`, `visibility:hidden`, or `aria-hidden="true"` (a deliberately-hidden drawer) is not an escape. Decide the rule, write it into `harness/responsive-spec.md`, and update the auditor and the gate together (they stay two independent encodings of one spec). This is part of the capstone's constitution work, not a bug to hide.

## Content (example data, hero-agency specific)

Reuse the roster from the mock (Silverwing, Dr. Ion, Vantablack, Aurora Vale, Magnetar, The Tinkerer, Halcyon, Rift, Ember Cho, Null, Grond, Ms. Meridian) with their power classes (Aerial, Energy, Psionic, Tech, Mutant, Cosmic, Enhanced), power index (0-100), status (Active/Injured/Reserve/MIA), clearance tier, mission counts, and success rates. Mark it plainly as example data. The specifics (threat tiers, power classes, clearance) are the detail that makes this a real console rather than a generic CRUD table.

@reference "../../styles.css"; /* slice:placeholder. The slice generator owns this screen: npx ng g slice --spec specs/hero.json --kinds form,manage replaces it. */ ---- --- name: slice-generator description: Generates domain entities, schema-driven forms, and manage (CRUD list) screens from a JSON spec instead of writing them by hand. Use before creating a model, a service, a zod form schema, an example-data file, a form component, or a table/cards list screen with create, edit, delete, search and filter. Run `ng generate slice --spec specs/.json`, then wire the result in. --- # Slice generator Three kinds of code in this app are generated, not hand-written: the domain entity (model, zod schema, service, example data), the schema-driven form component, and the manage screen (a routed CRUD list). You describe the entity once in a spec file and the `slice` schematic emits all of it in the house shape: sealed spartan primitives, signal forms with `validateStandardSchema`, a component-scoped ViewModel, icons registered with `provideIcons`, unit tests for the service and the ViewModel. If you are about to write a `*.model.ts`, a `*.schema.ts`, a `*.service.ts`, a `*-form` component under `src/app/ui/`, or a list screen with a table, a create/edit dialog and a delete confirmation, stop and write a spec instead. ## The workflow 1. Write or extend `specs/.json` (kebab-case file name, for example `specs/book.json`). It must be valid against `schematics/slice/spec.schema.json`. The schema checks structure; the schematic also checks the cross-field rules (field references, example rows, kinds) and prints every problem it finds. 2. Run `ng generate slice --spec specs/.json`. 3. Wire the result in by hand: add a navigation link to a manage screen, show entity data on a dashboard, build any bespoke screen on top of the generated service. 4. If a generated file needs a small addition, make it in place with Edit. If it has the wrong shape, change the spec and regenerate that kind with `ng generate slice --spec specs/.json --kinds --force`. Do not rewrite a generated file, move it, rename it or write a copy beside it: the next regeneration would erase the rewrite, and a copy drifts from the one the spec describes. When a file the run would write already exists, the schematic looks at it first. If it is identical to what the generator emits (line endings aside), it is skipped and the run prints `Unchanged: `, so rerunning over your own unchanged output is safe and changes nothing. If it carries the placeholder marker `slice:placeholder`, it is replaced without `--force`: a placeholder holds nothing you need (the starting app may hold one, such as `src/app/heroes/heroes.*`). Any other existing file stops the run: it fails with an `already exists` line for each such file and writes nothing, which protects hand-written code and your in-place edits. `--force` (the standard `ng generate` flag) replaces every such file the requested kinds produce. Use it only when every file it would replace is this generator's output or something you mean to lose, and pair it with `--kinds` so it touches only the kind whose shape you changed. Check with `git status --short ` for each file the run would replace: nothing is committed between stages, so every file a stage created is untracked and shows up there. If hand-written work you need is in the way, do not force: keep it and build on the generated service instead. The schematic reads its own source from `schematics/`. That folder is read-only for you: you can read it to understand an output, but a change to what the generator emits is not yours to make. Work through the spec. ## Generating one kind at a time `--kinds` takes a comma-separated subset of the spec's `kinds`, for example `ng generate slice --spec specs/loan.json --kinds entity` now and `--kinds form,manage` later. Without it, the run generates every kind the spec lists. A kind whose dependencies are not generated in the same run must find them on disk: `form` needs the entity's model, schema and service, and `manage` needs those plus the form component. If they are missing, the run stops, names the missing files and the command that makes them, and writes nothing. A kind the spec does not list is refused. ## Generated files Every TypeScript file the schematic writes starts with this line: // @generated by the slice schematic from its spec. Edit in place; reshape via the spec and --force. The generator writes, under `src/app/`, every `*.model.ts`, `*.schema.ts`, `*.service.ts`, `*.service.spec.ts` and `*-example-data.ts` of an entity, and everything under `ui/-form/`. In this app a hook enforces the part that marks a hand-built domain, but only for an entity that has a spec at `specs/.json` (for example `specs/book.json`): for that entity, a Write that creates its `*.model.ts`, `*.schema.ts` or `*-example-data.ts`, or any file under `ui/-form/`, is denied with the command that generates it. A Write over a file that carries `slice:placeholder` is denied whatever the entity. Hand-written schemas and models for features without an entity spec, such as a wizard's `.schema.ts`, are not policed. Services are not policed by the hook, because the app has services the generator does not make, such as a theme service; an entity's service still comes from the generator with the rest of the entity. Edit is allowed, so you fill and adjust generated files in place. After a shell command, the same hook reports any of those policed files that does not start with the header, because the generator did not write it. ## Order matters when entities reference each other A `ref` field imports the target entity's service. Generate the entity that is referenced first. If `loan` references `book` and `member`, generate `book` and `member` before `loan`, or `loan` will not compile. ## What each kind emits `entity` writes, under `src/app//`: - `.model.ts`: the interface and one string-union type per enum field. - `.schema.ts`: the zod schema (one entry per field with `inForm` true, with `.meta({...} satisfies FormFieldMeta)`), exporting `Schema` and `type FormModel = z.infer<...>`. - `.service.ts`: a root-provided `Service` with a private signal seeded from example data, a readonly list signal named after `plural`, `byId`, `create`, `update`, `remove`. If the entity has `ref` fields, the service also prunes references to records that no longer exist, and a many-ref field gets a `for(id)` lookup. - `-example-data.ts`: the spec's `examples`, marked as example data. Ids are assigned `"1"`, `"2"`, and so on, by row position. - `.service.spec.ts`: tests for seeding, create, update, remove, and reference pruning. `form` writes `src/app/ui/-form/-form.ts`, `-form.html` and `-form.css`: a standalone `Form` component built from the schema. It has one `hlm-field` block per form field, chosen by type, an `initialValue` input reseeded through a `linkedSignal` compared by value, a `save` output and a `cancel` output. A `ref` field also gets a `Options` input that the parent fills. `manage` writes, under `src/app//`, a routed screen: - `.ts`: a thin component with `providers: [ViewModel]`, `templateUrl` and `styleUrl`. - `.view-model.ts`: the ViewModel with search, the select and toggle filters, the optional sort, editing state, `startCreate`, `startEdit`, `cancel`, `save`, `remove`, and the option lists for ref fields. - `.html`: a table in a scroll container (no stacked cards), the select and toggle filters the spec asks for, an edit dialog hosting the generated form, a create dialog hosting it too (or, with `createRoute`, a create link instead), a delete confirmation dialog, an empty state, and, when the spec sets `summary`, a footer with a count, plus a "sorted by" line only when `sort` is also set. Classes are BEM on the `` block. - `.css`: a layout-only stylesheet for those BEM classes. - `.view-model.spec.ts`: ViewModel tests. - It also adds a lazy route for `plural` to `src/app/app.routes.ts`, unless a route already loads `.//` under any path: then it keeps that route and its path, and adds none. If it cannot find the `routes` array literal it stops with an error instead of guessing. ## What is not generated - Navigation. The route exists after generation; add the link to the shell yourself. - Dashboards, stat tiles, detail pages, tabs, wizards, settings screens, and any other bespoke screen. Build those by hand on top of the generated services, with their own ViewModels. - Cross-entity computed columns (for example a count of related records). Add a method to a hand-written ViewModel, or a bespoke screen. - Backend access. Services are in-memory and seeded from the example data. - More than three filters, clickable column sorting, avatar or custom cells, columns that show a `ref` field, and multi-select form controls. ## The spec A spec is pure data. <form class="hero-form" [formRoot]="heroForm">
  <hlm-field-group>
    <hlm-field>
      <label hlmFieldLabel for="name">{{ meta['name'].label }}</label>
      <input
        hlmInput
        id="name"
        [formField]="heroForm.name"
        [placeholder]="meta['name'].placeholder ?? ''"
      />
      <hlm-field-description>{{ meta['name'].help }}</hlm-field-description>
      @for (error of heroForm.name().errors(); track error) {
        <hlm-field-error [validator]="error.kind">{{ error.message }}</hlm-field-error>
      }
    </hlm-field>

    <hlm-field>
      <label hlmFieldLabel for="alias">{{ meta['alias'].label }}</label>
      <input
        hlmInput
        id="alias"
        [formField]="heroForm.alias"
        [placeholder]="meta['alias'].placeholder ?? ''"
      />
      <hlm-field-description>{{ meta['alias'].help }}</hlm-field-description>
      @for (error of heroForm.alias().errors(); track error) {
        <hlm-field-error [validator]="error.kind">{{ error.message }}</hlm-field-error>
      }
    </hlm-field>

    <hlm-field>
      <label hlmFieldLabel for="powerClass">{{ meta['powerClass'].label }}</label>
      <hlm-select [formField]="heroForm.powerClass" [itemToString]="powerClassToString">
        <hlm-select-trigger buttonId="powerClass" class="hero-form__select">
          <hlm-select-value [placeholder]="meta['powerClass'].placeholder ?? ''" />
        </hlm-select-trigger>
        <hlm-select-content *hlmSelectPortal>
          <hlm-select-group>
            <hlm-select-label>{{ meta['powerClass'].label }}</hlm-select-label>
            @for (option of powerClassOptions; track option.value) {
              <hlm-select-item [value]="option.value">{{ option.label }}</hlm-select-item>
            }
          </hlm-select-group>
        </hlm-select-content>
      </hlm-select>
      @for (error of heroForm.powerClass().errors(); track error) {
        <hlm-field-error [validator]="error.kind">{{ error.message }}</hlm-field-error>
      }
    </hlm-field>

    <hlm-field>
      <label hlmFieldLabel for="power">{{ meta['power'].label }}</label>
      <input hlmInput id="power" type="number" [formField]="heroForm.power" />
      <hlm-field-description>{{ meta['power'].help }}</hlm-field-description>
      @for (error of heroForm.power().errors(); track error) {
        <hlm-field-error [validator]="error.kind">{{ error.message }}</hlm-field-error>
      }
    </hlm-field>

    <hlm-field>
      <label hlmFieldLabel for="status">{{ meta['status'].label }}</label>
      <hlm-select [formField]="heroForm.status" [itemToString]="statusToString">
        <hlm-select-trigger buttonId="status" class="hero-form__select">
          <hlm-select-value [placeholder]="meta['status'].placeholder ?? ''" />
        </hlm-select-trigger>
        <hlm-select-content *hlmSelectPortal>
          <hlm-select-group>
            <hlm-select-label>{{ meta['status'].label }}</hlm-select-label>
            @for (option of statusOptions; track option.value) {
              <hlm-select-item [value]="option.value">{{ option.label }}</hlm-select-item>
            }
          </hlm-select-group>
        </hlm-select-content>
      </hlm-select>
      @for (error of heroForm.status().errors(); track error) {
        <hlm-field-error [validator]="error.kind">{{ error.message }}</hlm-field-error>
      }
    </hlm-field>

    <hlm-field>
      <label hlmFieldLabel for="clearance">{{ meta['clearance'].label }}</label>
      <hlm-select [formField]="heroForm.clearance" [itemToString]="clearanceToString">
        <hlm-select-trigger buttonId="clearance" class="hero-form__select">
          <hlm-select-value [placeholder]="meta['clearance'].placeholder ?? ''" />
        </hlm-select-trigger>
        <hlm-select-content *hlmSelectPortal>
          <hlm-select-group>
            <hlm-select-label>{{ meta['clearance'].label }}</hlm-select-label>
            @for (option of clearanceOptions; track option.value) {
              <hlm-select-item [value]="option.value">{{ option.label }}</hlm-select-item>
            }
          </hlm-select-group>
        </hlm-select-content>
      </hlm-select>
      @for (error of heroForm.clearance().errors(); track error) {
        <hlm-field-error [validator]="error.kind">{{ error.message }}</hlm-field-error>
      }
    </hlm-field>

    <hlm-field>
      <label hlmFieldLabel for="notes">{{ meta['notes'].label }}</label>
      <textarea
        hlmTextarea
        id="notes"
        rows="4"
        [formField]="heroForm.notes"
        [placeholder]="meta['notes'].placeholder ?? ''"
      ></textarea>
      <hlm-field-description>{{ meta['notes'].help }}</hlm-field-description>
      @for (error of heroForm.notes().errors(); track error) {
        <hlm-field-error [validator]="error.kind">{{ error.message }}</hlm-field-error>
      }
    </hlm-field>

    <hlm-field>
      <label hlmFieldLabel class="hero-form__switch">
        <hlm-switch [formField]="heroForm.active" />
        {{ meta['active'].label }}
      </label>
      @for (error of heroForm.active().errors(); track error) {
        <hlm-field-error [validator]="error.kind">{{ error.message }}</hlm-field-error>
      }
    </hlm-field>

    <hlm-field orientation="horizontal">
      <button hlmBtn type="submit">{{ submitLabel() }}</button>
      <button hlmBtn type="button" variant="outline" (click)="cancel.emit()">Cancel</button>
    </hlm-field>
  </hlm-field-group>
</form>

content.text:
The roster screen is generated and finished, and `ng build` compiles. Lint is clean and the 13 roster ViewModel tests pass.

**What the generator wrote**
- `src/app/ui/hero-form/` (form component), and the roster files in `src/app/heroes/`, replacing the placeholder. The existing `./heroes/heroes` route is kept, and no second route was added.

**What I changed by hand, against the build spec's roster diagram**
- **Recruit button** moved onto the filter row, next to the class filter, as in the diagram. It stays a link to `/recruit`, since the spec sets `createRoute`.
- **Hero cell** now shows an `hlm-avatar` monogram, the name, and the alias underneath. The spec's "Name/ID" column is shown as name and alias because hero ids are row numbers (`"1"`, `"2"`) and mean nothing to a reader. Say if you want the id instead.
- **Edit dialog** now has `(closed)="vm.cancel()"`. Before, Escape, the close button, or an outside click left the record set as "being edited". `cancel` was also a method no template called.
- **Removed `startCreate`** and the create branch of `save`. The generator emitted them, but creation goes to `/recruit`, so nothing called them. The spec file's create-through-save test is replaced by tests for the dismiss reset and the monogram.
- **Stylesheet** holds the BEM layout classes only. The search box has no icon, matching the diagram. A leading icon would need padding on the vendored input, which the app-CSS gate rejects, and no input-group primitive is vendored.

The table already sits in an `overflow-x: auto` container, which is the spec's answer (a) for 375px.

**Not verified**
- `check:wiring` could not run: `harness/counter/` is not on disk, so the script fails with "module not found". I checked by hand that every public ViewModel member is referenced by the template.
- `check:boot`, `check:interaction`, `check:responsive` and `check:contrast` were not run, so there is no browser check at 375 / 768 / 1280 yet.
- The dismiss wiring cannot be exercised in jsdom. Its unit test calls `cancel()` directly, which would pass even with the template unwired.
- The build prints a budget warning: the initial bundle is 589 kB against a 500 kB budget. The lazy `heroes` chunk is 534 kB raw. I did not investigate either size, and I did not check whether the warning predates this change.
